lines: Mind the lectern. It has heard better questions than most people ask.
Give the lectern room. Records works better without elbows in it.
Step carefully near the lectern. I would rather greet you than patch you up.
There you are. I was just near the lectern, trying to keep the day sensible.
Morning. Or afternoon. The work makes the hours blur if I let it.
Good to see you walking in calmly. That usually means nothing is on fire yet.
If you need me, speak up. If you need gossip, speak quieter.
You caught me before the next little disaster. That is rare timing.
Hello. Try not to bring the whole village into this unless it is important.
I have a moment. Not a long one, but a real one.
Lower your voice a little. The shelves are dramatic today.
Hello. If you borrowed something, begin with honesty.
You caught me between pages, which is safer than between arguments.
Mind the lectern. It holds grudges through splinters.
Welcome. Clean hands make better readers.
I have a moment, provided nobody has shelved farming under danger again.
Come in quietly or at least thoughtfully.
The books are settled. Let us see if people can match them.
If you need an answer, tell me whether you want quick or correct.
Good timing. I was losing a debate with a footnote.
Hello there. Do not fold the corners of anything alive or paper.
I am listening, though the margin was speaking first.
Stand away from the open ink and near your better judgment.
You look like a question with boots.
I can spare a short chapter of attention.
